title: committed plan records carry no machine path, and the committed-artifact check reads the plan
description: A phase shard's task text named scratch files by their absolute path on the machine that wrote them, and nothing flagged it because the committed-artifact check does not read the plan. Extend its domain to the plan, red first, then scrub the two shards it finds; words that quote a matched shape are avoided in this phase's own text.
desiredOutcome: tools/check-committed-pii.py scans the plan index and every phase shard, and no committed plan record names a path inside a user's home directory or the machine's temporary directory

tasks.title: the committed-artifact check reads the plan, and the shards it finds are scrubbed
tasks.description: Extend check-committed-pii's derived domain to the plan: the index and every file under docs/audit/phases. Red first with a synthetic shard that names a path inside a home directory and one inside the temporary directory. Run the extended check over the real tree BEFORE deciding anything else, and report every hit. Scrub the hits in P85 and P86 by replacing each absolute scratch path with the file's base name (the text keeps what it pointed at). Any other hit is reported, not baselined, until the orchestrator decides. No verb rewrites a finished task's description, so the scrub is this task's own declared edit.

add: tools/check-committed-pii.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a phase shard or the plan index naming a machine path is outside the check's domain and so is never found

outcome.technical: tools/check-committed-pii.py: plan_files derives the index from the plugin config's manifestPath and the shards from the index's own pointers (surface 'plan'); plan-index-unparseable and plan-config-unreadable findings; q24/q25 fixture, q6 expects the plan surface; BASELINE rows keyed by path, line and detector with reasons. P85 (done tasks, direct edit) and P86 (pending tasks, scope --description) scrubbed to the base name.
outcome.descriptive: The committed-artifact check reads the plan index and every phase shard; the two shards that named the machine's scratch directory now name the file alone, and every other hit, a quoted example shape, is baselined with its reason.

intentCheck.basis: the scrub of P85/P86 was made by the orchestrator with the owner's approval (the plan gate refuses a subagent's plan write), not by this task's executor; the domain extension and the baseline are the executor's
